author: Morison, Samuel Eliot
title: History of United States Naval Operations in World War II, Volume V: The Struggle for Guadalcanal, August 1942 – February 1943
publisher: Little, Brown and Company, Boston (an Atlantic Monthly Press book)
notes: The seven naval actions of the Guadalcanal campaign — Savo Island, the Eastern Solomons, Cape Esperance, Santa Cruz, the two nights of the naval battle of Guadalcanal, Tassafaronga and Rennell Island — which ADR 0019 keeps inside one pack rather than splitting into seven. The year is not what the catalogues say. Every catalogue consulted (Open Library, Wikipedia, the standard series lists) dates this volume 1949; the copyright page of the 1958 printing reads 'Copyright 1948 … Published September 1948 … Reprinted October 1948', which cannot be reconciled with a 1949 publication, and the printing history matches source:morison-vol-3's line for line, as two volumes issued together would. The item is followed here over the catalogue, but the conflict is unresolved and anyone with a first printing in hand should settle it. Morison's Savo Island is the part of this volume later work argues with: he wrote close to the event and to the officers involved, and source:frank-1990 and source:toll-2015 reach a different distribution of blame. See source:morison-vol-3 for the note on the series.
